summary.headline: H.G. Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT swung to a loss of INR45 crores on revenue of INR1,101 crores; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 13.5-14%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was a weak quarter: standalone revenue of INR907 crores with EBITDA of INR77 crores (8.49% margin) and PAT of INR28 crores, versus PAT of INR125 crores a year earlier. Consolidated revenue was INR1,101 crores with EBITDA of INR304 crores (27.6%, lifted by solar receipts), but consolidated PAT was a loss of INR45 crores, including an exceptional item tied to Raipur OD5/OD6 SPVs and AP-1 discounting. Management blamed project-specific execution delays (appointed dates, pondage, bitumen/HSD supply, land and ROW for BESS/transmission) and said most issues are now under control. Guidance for FY27 revenue was cut to a range of INR6,000-6,500 crores, with recovery expected in H2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR125 crores (7.34% margin) in Q1 FY26
Boosted by solar receipts of roughly INR50 crores billed to DISCOM

financial_highlights.value: Negative INR45 crores (PAT margin stated as 4.04%)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR99 crores (6.7% margin) in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR1,834 crores (WC debt INR910 crores, NCD INR400 crores, term loans and CMTL INR524 crores)
INR14,502 crores (roads and highways INR9,386 crores; rail/metro INR3,054 crores; transmission and distribution INR1,457 crores; BESS INR461 crores; solar INR144 crores)

segments.name: Roads and highways (EPC and HAM)
segments.commentary: Order book of INR9,386 crores, about 65% of total. Pune-Shirur (INR3,931 crores, from Welspun) is in mobilisation with appointed date expected around October 2026; Karnal Ring Road is 99% complete; Raipur-Visakhapatnam OD5/OD6 and AP-1 and Khammam-Devarapalli KD1/KD2 have provisional completion with COD targeted in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Railways and metro
segments.commentary: Order book of INR3,054 crores, about 21% of total. DMRC Metro at 100% completion (in handover); Bilaspur RVNL at 99%, targeted Q2 FY27; New Delhi stations at 13.34%; Thane Metro faces land and local disruption issues. Two Adani thermal-plant rail projects (Anuppur INR340 crores, Mirzapur INR440 crores) are being mobilised.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Physical progress about 94% as of 30 June 2026; order book INR144 crores. Around INR175 crores invoiced to state DISCOMs for 137 commissioned plants; target annual revenue of INR250 crores-plus on full commissioning. About INR300 crores-plus of project debt still to be released post commissioning. KUSUM Rajasthan deadline extended to 31 March 2027.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Order book of INR461 crores. Binding agreement with GUVNL and NVVN for 735 MW / 1,470 MWh across 3 projects; procurement for 435 MW almost complete, with DC block container order placed with CATL. Banaskantha and Dholera targeted for February and March 2027, Choraniya for June 2027; expected annual revenue about INR225 crores.

segments.name: Transmission and distribution
segments.commentary: Order book of INR1,457 crores. Odisha transmission project has financial closure and long-lead items placed. Two RECPDCL projects (Mirzapur EPC INR320 crores; Jamshedpur EPC INR843 crores) expected to generate about INR215 crores annual revenue over a 35-year concession.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR6,000-6,500 crores (versus earlier mention of at least INR6,100 crores, the FY25 level); Q2 FY27 revenue expected at roughly INR1,000 crores.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 13.5-14%, with H2 margins expected around 15%-plus as employee cost is absorbed by higher revenue.
FY28 revenue targeted at about INR7,000 crores; FY28 margin of 13.5-14% described as doable, supported by transmission projects with 13-15% EPC margin.
FY27 order inflow targeted at INR11,000-12,000 crores, of which about INR5,500 crores already received in Q1 FY27.

Standalone external debt target of INR900 crores by year-end, from INR1,834 crores at June 2026, funded by receivables and about INR800-850 crores of monetisation proceeds; working capital targeted at around 50 days by year-end.

Equity infusion remaining of about INR583 crores for the rest of FY27, INR625 crores in FY28 and INR146 crores in FY29 (total about INR1,354 crores), against about INR1,664-1,665 crores already infused.
capex_capacity: Solar: about 94% physical progress; remaining plants to be commissioned over coming months within revised contract timelines.
BESS: three projects with 735 MW / 1,470 MWh; Banaskantha and Dholera commissioning Feb and Mar 2027, Choraniya June 2027; civil works progressing and land acquired through SPV.
Transmission: Odisha project with financial closure, procurement underway; two RECPDCL projects newly secured.

HAM monetisation: KD1 51% and OD5 49% sold in Q1 (partial consideration INR70 crores and INR140 crores); OD6 100% sold (INR203 crores); OD5 remaining 51% sold in July 2026 (INR103 crores); AP-1 equity transfer expected in the upcoming quarter; Karnal HAM monetisation expected by year-end.
Completed EPC: Ganga Expressway and UER, with COD being obtained. Jamshedpur elevated at 61.12%; Nelamangala-Tumakuru at 70%, likely complete by March 2027; DLF project at 3% due to land constraints.
demand_pricing: Management cited muted project awarding and bidding activity, geopolitical uncertainty, intensifying competition and lower margins as industry headwinds.
Bids submitted till date: about INR22,000 crores in HAM and highways, about INR4,000 crores in rail, and one or two transmission bids.
NHAI plans 54 projects worth about INR1.85 lakh crores for award in FY27; management also sees rail/metro (high-speed and Namo Bharat) and transmission opportunities.

About INR6,000-plus crores of the INR14,500 crore order book is not yet executable (Pune-Shirur, Odisha Capital Region Ring Road, and a Mirzapur project, plus a transmission project), with appointed dates expected around October 2026.
Employee cost rose to 10.3% of revenue from 5.4% (as cited by an analyst), which management attributed to low revenue on delayed HAM and Ganga projects.

qa_highlights.question: Why were margins hit in Q1 and what is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar margins were hit by transmission-line and ROW issues, plant relocation and higher transmission line cost. FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 13.5-14%, with H2 around 15%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 revenue guidance of INR6,100-6,500 crores realistic given Q1 of INR907 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept a INR6,000-6,500 crore range: about INR1,000 crores in Q2, about INR3,000 crores from highways in H2 (including about INR700 crores from Pune-Shirur and about INR150 crores from Odisha), at least INR600 crores from BESS and transmission, and about INR2,000 crores from rail.

qa_highlights.question: What are the equity requirements for HAM, BESS and transmission?
qa_highlights.answer: Total equity requirement is about INR1,689 crores for solar/BESS/transmission (INR959 crores invested) and INR1,331 crores for HAM (about INR750 crores invested). Remaining: about INR583 crores in 9M FY27, INR625 crores in FY28 and INR146 crores in FY29 (figures given varied during the call).

qa_highlights.question: When will the operational claims settlements and monetisation cash come in?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR42 crores settled with INR29 crores received in July; about INR100 crores expected in September from a ministry claim; around INR200 crores more from other claims by year-end. Monetisation of about INR660 crores received, INR725 crores pending, with about INR250 crores in Q2 and the rest in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt will come down in 12 months from project cash flows alone?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR300 crores-plus from operating cash flows, plus INR300 crores-plus of solar SPV debt release, against about INR800 crores monetisation covering INR583 crores equity need; total cash receivables about INR900 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated EBITDA margin rise despite lower revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to solar receipts (about INR50 crores billed to DISCOM) that carry almost no operating cost; solar, BESS and transmission together are expected to add INR650-700 crores of annual EBITDA once commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable share of the order book and what changed in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR6,000-plus crores of the INR14,500 crore order book is not executable; about INR8,000 crores is executable. Q2 execution improving at Varanasi-Kolkata, Anuppur and a INR200 crore variation in Delhi-Vadodara; Q3-Q4 expected to be more aggressive.

risks_watch: Revenue guidance of INR6,000-6,500 crores requires about INR5,100-5,600 crores in Q2-Q4 after Q1 standalone revenue of INR907 crores; Q2 is guided at roughly INR1,000 crores, and analysts questioned whether the low end is reachable.

About INR6,000-plus crores of the INR14,500 crore order book is not yet executable (Pune-Shirur, Odisha ring road, a Mirzapur project and a transmission project), with appointed dates expected around October 2026; any slip pushes H2 revenue further out.

Margin recovery to 13.5-14% for FY27 depends on H2 EBITDA margins of about 15%-plus; Q2 is expected to stay weak because of monsoon and supply disruption, and employee cost is 10.3% of revenue versus 5.4% earlier.

Debt reduction to INR900 crores by year-end (from INR1,834 crores) relies on about INR800-850 crores of monetisation, of which about INR725 crores was still pending, plus INR300 crores-plus of solar SPV debt release that has slipped before.

Equity requirement of about INR583 crores for the rest of FY27, with figures given inconsistently during the call (INR1,664 crores vs INR959 crores vs INR750 crores infused in different segments); the CFO-level reconciliation was not provided.

Exceptional item tied to Raipur OD5/OD6 SPVs and AP-1 discounting drove the consolidated PAT loss; net debt and gross debt on a consolidated basis, and balance sheet receivables detail, were deferred to the IR team.
key_quotes: Just to highlight here, last year was not as per our expectations.
I would like to convey that most of these issues are now under control, and we are working towards regaining the desired execution momentum.

So overall, this margin front that definitely the project which we've already have started in highways and rail projects, say 1 or 2 projects where the margins are not that encouraging. But overall margin would be in the range of about 13.5% to 14% EBITDA level.
Harendra Singh: So these details, I will tell my team to connect to you because now I'm not having immediately with me.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid that Q1 FY27 was disappointing and attributed the shortfall to project-specific and external factors, while stating that most issues are now under control. Confidence was high on H2 recovery and FY27 guidance, but it was cautious on Q2 and was evasive on several specifics: it deferred balance-sheet, net debt and debt-to-equity questions to the IR team and gave inconsistent equity figures.
